cases.name: grouping-key-collision-stale-upstream-cache
cases.boundary: OCaml rebuilds roles after joined-key collision removal; Go removes the caller tuple from the role cache and leaves the removed stored tuple active.

cases.name: strict-policy-arity-two-fields
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects wrong-arity p operations atomically; Go stores the short row, exposes it in queries, and fails later enforcement until it is removed.

cases.name: strict-policy-arity-four-fields
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects oversized p rules before mutation; Go stores them and reports an enforcement size error.

cases.name: strict-grouping-short-row
cases.boundary: Go returns an error for a short g add but leaves the malformed row stored until removal; OCaml rejects before mutation. Wrong-arity query/remove calls are also rejected by OCaml.

cases.name: strict-grouping-extra-field
cases.boundary: OCaml requires exactly two grouping fields. Go stores extra fields but builds a role link using only the first two.

cases.name: strict-grouping-cycle-preserves-state
cases.boundary: Raw Go grouping mutations accept cycles. OCaml validates the candidate graph and retains the previous snapshot on rejection.

cases.name: strict-self-edge-preserves-state
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects explicit self edges while preserving implicit self membership. Raw Go mutations store the edge.

cases.name: duplicate-before-self-cycle-validation
cases.note: The comma-key identity already exists under a distinct valid tuple. Adding a key-colliding self tuple is a no-op, so graph validation must occur only after the duplicate check.

cases.name: domain-cycle-mutating-one-domain
cases.boundary: OCaml validates cycles independently per domain, accepting opposing edges in separate domains but rejecting a newly closed same-domain cycle. Go accepts the in-memory cycle.

cases.name: domain-self-edge-atomic
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects explicit domain self edges atomically, retaining implicit self membership; raw Go accepts and exposes the stored edge.

cases.name: domain-collision-removal-stale-cache
cases.boundary: Comma-joined grouping identity can collide across different domain tuples. Go removes the caller-domain link from its incremental cache, retaining the removed stored-domain edge; OCaml rebuilds from stored rows.

cases.name: domain-wrong-pair-arity-atomic
cases.boundary: Go reports an add error for a short domain grouping row but leaves it stored until removal. OCaml rejects arity before mutation and rejects pair operations on a domain model.

cases.name: domain-explicit-query-requires-domain-model
cases.boundary: Explicit OCaml domain queries require a three-field g definition. Pinned two-field Go role managers ignore extra domain arguments and return ordinary links.

cases.name: domain-nul-memo-key-collision
cases.boundary: Pinned GenerateGFunction concatenates NUL-separated arguments without escaping NUL bytes inside values. Distinct domain tuples can share a memo key and incorrectly reuse membership. OCaml evaluates the consistent exact-byte graph and does not emulate the cached incorrect grant.

cases.name: priority-invalid-additions-atomic
cases.boundary: Go stores nonnumeric/out-of-range priorities and appends them; OCaml validates newly stored priorities atomically. Has/remove remain raw-key operations and return false for each rejected row. Both states return to empty after the corresponding Go removal.
